Jira issues and Confluence pages on the sites the person grants.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Atlassian account in each app that uses it, for the scopes that app lists. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

The redirect URI to register, with your Gateway's address (like `apps.example.com`):

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/atlassian/callback
```

Calls go to api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/&lt;cloud id>/… ; the cloud id comes from /oauth/token/accessible-resources.

1. Open [developer.atlassian.com](https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/) and create an OAuth app (also called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Copy the client ID and client secret. The secret is often shown only once.

Add it to your Gateway. It asks for the client ID and secret:

```bash
everyapp provider add atlassian
```

Or add it in **Manage workspace → Providers**.

### Use it in an app

List the provider's own scopes in the app's `everyapp.config.ts`:

```ts
capabilities: {
  atlassian: { scopes: ["read:jira-work"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

Use [Atlassian's scopes](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/scopes-for-oauth-2-3LO-and-forge-apps/). The Gateway adds `read:me`, `offline_access` itself; don't list them. The app calls Atlassian's API with `integrationFetch()`, and the Gateway adds the person's token. A token with more scopes than the app lists is refused.

**Check it worked:** `everyapp provider show atlassian` shows the client as set. Then open an app that lists it and select its **Connect** button.

Something wrong or missing? [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Atlassian%20%28Jira%20and%20Confluence%29).
